label: Postgres: Watch query
description: Keep a query's result live: run it now and on a cadence, and send the rows on the `rows` bus each time they differ from last time (pipe it into a Stream behind a Route for a live page). Parameters are inline-declared input ports read by name (`$user_id`), as in Postgres: Query; one statement only. With `channel` set it also LISTENs, so a `NOTIFY` from the database re-runs the query at once. A declared output port named after a column (`-> (count: Bus)`) gets that column of the first row as its own bus, so `select count(*)` sends `7` rather than `[{"count": 7}]`. A tick with no rows sends nothing on those ports and leaves them open. Runs until the run ends, then the buses close.

inputs.name: account
inputs.description: Wire a PostgresAccess, or a PostgresDatabase's access output.

inputs.name: query
inputs.label: SQL
inputs.placeholder: SELECT id, caption FROM cards ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50
inputs.description: The one statement to keep live; each `$name` reads the input port of that name.

inputs.name: intervalSecs
inputs.label: Every (seconds)
inputs.description: Seconds between re-runs (at least 5): the whole cadence, or the backstop when `channel` is set.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.label: Notify channel
inputs.description: NOTIFY channel to LISTEN on; each notification re-runs the query. Empty polls only. Raise it from a database trigger whose function calls `pg_notify('cards_changed', '')`.

outputs.name: rows
outputs.description: One message per change carrying the whole row list (the first right after start).

then.message: '{id}' aliases a column to `rows`, which is this node's own output (the whole result, on a bus). A column of that name has nowhere to go. Alias it to something else in the SQL and declare a port for that name.
